beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Editing a video means learning the timeline — the cuts, the tracks, the little keyframe diamonds. Or it did. Because the next version of the editor doesn't ask you to learn anything. It asks you to just say what you want.

beats.narration_text: Four terms, before we start. Shorts: YouTube's short, vertical videos. YouTube Create: YouTube's free editing app for your phone. Chat editing: an AI editor you instruct in plain language, inside a chat window. Edits: Meta's own video-editing app.

terms.meaning: YouTube's free editing app for phones
an AI editor you instruct in plain language

beats.narration_text: Picture a chat window sitting inside your editing app. You type: match the cuts to the beat. And the clips rearrange themselves — no timeline, no dragging, no keyframes. That is the whole idea: an editor that takes instructions in plain language.

shot.visual_intent: A phone; its chat window; your instruction 'match the cuts to the beat' lands as a bubble; the film strip below shuffles its clips into a new order on its own.

show.event: user bubble 'match the cuts to the beat' lands
film-strip clips shuffle into a new order

beats.narration_text: Why does this matter? Because editing eats time. The creator who demoed this for YouTube put it this way: a one-hour shoot can be ten hours or more in the edit. Ten hours of trimming, cutting, and nudging clips into place.

shot.visual_intent: A timeline crowded with tiny clips; a '1 hour shoot' card becomes a '10+ hours edit' card as a clock hand spins.

show.event: clock spins; '10+ hours edit' card lands

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat B01: one drawing, minimal labels

beats.narration_text: So here is what YouTube announced at its Made on YouTube event this September: a conversational editing assistant, coming to Shorts and to the YouTube Create app. You start from a suggested prompt, or type your own — then keep refining the cut by continuing the conversation.

shot.visual_intent: A 'Made on YouTube · Sept 2026' card; a phone slides in carrying a chat window; 'Shorts' and 'YouTube Create' labels dock beneath it.

show.event: phone with chat window slides in

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat B02: one drawing, minimal labels

beats.narration_text: In YouTube's demo, the creator Happy Kelli hands over dance footage — herself dancing, in different outfits. She asks the assistant to pick the best take of each outfit. Then she says: add music, add transitions. And the assistant assembles the cut.

shot.visual_intent: Three 'take' cards (outfit A, B, C); the chat picks the best of each; a music note and transition arrows land on the assembled cut.

chat bubble 'best take of each outfit' lands
best takes lift out; also-rans dim
music note + transition arrows land on the cut

beats.narration_text: It handles the fiddly work too. Text overlays, on command. Pauses in speech, removed. And it makes suggestions from the conversation itself — it reads what you are going for, and proposes the next move.

shot.visual_intent: A chat bubble; a text-overlay chip stamps onto a clip; pause gaps shrink on a waveform; suggestion chips fan out below.

show.event: text overlay stamps onto a clip
pause gaps shrink on the waveform

beats.narration_text: And here is the part that matters most: at any point, you can jump back into the regular timeline and adjust everything by hand. The AI drafts; you direct. As the demo put it: it edits with you, not for you.

shot.visual_intent: The chat window slides aside; the real timeline appears; a cursor drags a clip edge by hand; the tag 'edits with you, not for you' lands.

'edits with you, not for you' tag lands

beats.narration_text: When can you try it? The reported window is early twenty twenty-seven — for Shorts and the Create app. It is a preview today, not a product. But the direction is set: the timeline stops being the price of admission.

shot.visual_intent: A calendar page turns to a hero tag reading 'early 2027'; 'Shorts' and 'Create app' labels dock beneath; a timeline icon fades behind a 'no longer required' ring.

beats.narration_text: Meanwhile, Meta has already shipped its version of the idea, inside the Edits app. Announced September thirtieth and rolling out in the US: an assistant that reads your Reels numbers — views, watch time, likes — and suggests what to make next.

shot.visual_intent: An 'Edits' phone; dashboard bars for views, watch time, likes grow; a chat bubble assembles from the bars carrying 'what to make next'.

'what to make next' lands in the bubble

beats.narration_text: Hooks, captions, scripts — it can even suggest trending audio. But Meta draws a clear line: the assistant does the digging, it says. The creative calls stay yours.

shot.visual_intent: Suggestion chips (hooks, captions, scripts, audio) fan out; a divider line draws; below it the tag 'the creative calls stay yours' lands with a terracotta check.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat B08: one drawing, minimal labels

beats.narration_text: And you do not have to wait to start. The YouTube Create app already ships an AI first draft: it trims your clips and arranges them into a starting cut, all by itself. Same app — just no chat window yet. The conversation is the part that arrives in twenty twenty-seven.

shot.visual_intent: A 'YouTube Create' phone; loose clips auto-arrange into a first draft; a 'no chat yet' note appears, then a small 'chat: 2027' chip docks beside it.

show.event: loose clips auto-arrange into a first draft

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Act as my video editor. I will describe my footage. Reply with plain-language edit instructions, one per line: which parts to cut, where the music should shift, and what text to put on screen. My footage — then describe your clips. Check the result two ways. One: every instruction names exactly one thing to change. Two: a human editor could follow your list and ask no questions.
